```{python}
#| echo: false
from _common import *
import glob, io, zipfile
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
```

gdalxarray passes the string you give it to GDAL unchanged, so
everything GDAL's virtual file systems and connection strings can
express is available without any code in gdalxarray. This page walks
through the common ones using fixtures, so it runs anywhere.

| Prefix or syntax | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/vsicurl/<url>` | HTTP(S) range requests |
| `/vsis3/<bucket>/<key>`, `/vsigs/`, `/vsiaz/` | object stores (anonymous with `AWS_NO_SIGN_REQUEST=YES`) |
| `/vsizip/<zip>/<member>` | a member of a zip, which can itself be remote |
| `ZARR:"<store>":/<array>[:i:j]` | one array of a Zarr store, optionally a 2D slice of it |
| `NETCDF:"<file>":<var>` | one variable of a netCDF as a classic raster |
| `vrt://<path>?<options>` | an inline VRT: resize, subset, assign a CRS, pick bands |

## The same store, three addresses

A local directory, the same directory with the explicit `ZARR:` prefix,
and the same commit of the fixture over HTTPS all give the same
Dataset:

```{python}
rel = "cf/oisst-like.zarr"
addresses = {
    "local": fixture(rel),
    "ZARR: local": f'ZARR:"{fixture(rel)}"',
    "ZARR: /vsicurl/": f'ZARR:"{fixture(rel, remote=True)}"',
}
addresses["ZARR: /vsicurl/"]
```

```{python}
opened = {k: xr.open_dataset(v, engine="gdalxarray") for k, v in addresses.items()}
ref = opened["local"]["sst"].isel(time=1).values
{k: bool(np.array_equal(d["sst"].isel(time=1).values, ref, equal_nan=True)) for k, d in opened.items()}
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
for k, d in opened.items():
    assert np.array_equal(d["sst"].isel(time=1).values, ref, equal_nan=True), k
```

For a remote Zarr the `ZARR:` prefix is not optional. A web server has
no directory listing to sniff, so a bare `/vsicurl/.../store.zarr`
does not identify as anything:

```{python}
try:
    xr.open_dataset(fixture(rel, remote=True), engine="gdalxarray")
except Exception as e:
    print(type(e).__name__, str(e).splitlines()[0][:100])
```

Over `/vsicurl/`, also set `GDAL_DISABLE_READDIR_ON_OPEN=EMPTY_DIR` so
GDAL does not try to list what is really a web server. This site sets
it for every page.

## A 2D face of an N-D array

`ZARR:"store":/array:i:j` fixes the leading dimensions of an array to
indices `i`, `j`, leaving a 2D raster that classic tools understand.
Here `sst` is `(time, zlev, lat, lon)`, and `:2:0` picks the third day:

```{python}
face = xr.open_dataset(f'ZARR:"{fixture(rel)}":/sst:2:0', engine="gdalxarray", multidim=False)
face["band_data"].dims, face["band_data"].shape
```

The stored values are identical to the multidim read of the same
day:

```{python}
raw_face = xr.open_dataset(f'ZARR:"{fixture(rel)}":/sst:2:0', engine="gdalxarray",
                           multidim=False, mask_and_scale=False)["band_data"].values[0]
raw_md = xr.open_dataset(fixture(rel), engine="gdalxarray",
                         mask_and_scale=False)["sst"].isel(time=2, zlev=0).values
assert np.array_equal(raw_face, raw_md)
bool(np.array_equal(raw_face, raw_md))
```

but the two models can disagree on the fill value. This store was
written by xarray as Zarr v3, which puts the CF `_FillValue` (-999) in
the array's attributes while the Zarr-level `fill_value` is 0. GDAL
reports the Zarr-level value as the band or array nodata; gdalxarray's
multidim path prefers the CF attribute, and the classic path has only
GDAL's band value to go on:

```{python}
{"classic": face["band_data"].encoding.get("_FillValue"),
 "multidim": opened["local"]["sst"].encoding.get("_FillValue")}
```

With mask-and-scale decoding on, the classic face therefore masks
zeros rather than -999. Pass `mask_and_scale=False` and decode
yourself, or prefer the multidim read, for stores written this way.

## A netCDF variable, either way

The OISST-shaped netCDF fixtures can be opened as a multidimensional
dataset, or one variable as a classic raster with `NETCDF:`:

```{python}
nc = fixture("mdimrefs/nc/198109/oisst-avhrr-v02r01.19810901.nc")
md = xr.open_dataset(nc, engine="gdalxarray")
cl = xr.open_dataset(f'NETCDF:"{nc}":sst', engine="gdalxarray", multidim=False)
md["sst"].dims, cl["band_data"].dims
```

The two models differ in one way worth knowing: classic mode presents
the raster north-up (GDAL flips a south-up netCDF to give a
conventional geotransform), while multidim keeps the storage order.

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "The same netCDF variable: multidim keeps latitude ascending as stored; classic is north-up."
fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 2.8), layout="constrained")
axs[0].imshow(md["sst"].isel(time=0, zlev=0).values, cmap="RdYlBu_r")
axs[0].set_title(f"multidim: lat[0] = {float(md.lat[0])}")
axs[1].imshow(cl["band_data"].isel(band=0).values, cmap="RdYlBu_r")
axs[1].set_title(f"classic: y[0] = {float(cl.y[0])}")
for ax in axs:
    ax.set_xticks([]); ax.set_yticks([])
plt.show()
```

```{python}
assert np.array_equal(md["sst"].isel(time=0, zlev=0).values[::-1],
                      cl["band_data"].isel(band=0).values, equal_nan=True)
```

## Inline VRT options with `vrt://`

`vrt://` wraps a source in a VRT built from URL-style options, no XML
needed. A quarter-size average, and a window by coordinates:

```{python}
cog = fixture("cog/world-int16-deflate.tif")
full = xr.open_dataset(cog, engine="gdalxarray", multidim=False)
small = xr.open_dataset(f"vrt://{cog}?outsize=25%,25%&r=average", engine="gdalxarray", multidim=False)
win = xr.open_dataset(f"vrt://{cog}?projwin=100,-10,160,-50", engine="gdalxarray", multidim=False)
{k: d["band_data"].shape for k, d in dict(full=full, small=small, window=win).items()}
```

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "One COG through three vrt:// recipes: as is, a quarter-size average, and a projwin."
fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(12, 3), layout="constrained",
                        gridspec_kw=dict(width_ratios=[2, 2, 1]))
for ax, (name, d) in zip(axs, dict(full=full, small=small, window=win).items()):
    d["band_data"].isel(band=0).plot(ax=ax, add_colorbar=False, cmap="cividis")
    ax.set_title(f"{name} {d['band_data'].shape[1:]}")
plt.show()
```

The window keeps real coordinates, so it lines up with the full
raster:

```{python}
assert np.array_equal(win["band_data"].values,
                      full["band_data"].sel(x=win.x, y=win.y, method="nearest").values)
```

## Inside a zip

`/vsizip/` reads a member of a zip without unpacking it, and the zip
can be on a server (`/vsizip//vsicurl/https://...`). Here the zip is
built in memory:

```{python}
buf = io.BytesIO()
with zipfile.ZipFile(buf, "w") as z:
    z.writestr("day1.nc", fixture_bytes(
        "mdimrefs/nc/198109/oisst-avhrr-v02r01.19810901.nc"))
gdal.FileFromMemBuffer("/vsimem/days.zip", buf.getvalue())

zipped = xr.open_dataset("/vsizip//vsimem/days.zip/day1.nc", engine="gdalxarray")
bool(np.array_equal(zipped["sst"].values, md["sst"].values, equal_nan=True))
```

The [OISST gallery page](../gallery/oisst.qmd) uses the remote form: a
zipped multidimensional VRT on GitHub releases describing 45 years of
daily files on AWS.
